title: Stockroom
summary: A small warehouse service: stock levels per SKU and all-or-nothing order fulfilment.

tasks.title: Orders that list a SKU twice
brief: Support reports that a customer order failed with OutOfStock, yet some of its units still left the shelf. The order listed the same mug twice: two lines of 2 against a shelf of 3.
Orders are meant to be all or nothing. Find out why this one was not, fix it, and leave a test behind so it stays fixed.
done: A failed order never changes any stock level.
Orders that repeat a SKU are judged on the total they ask for.

questions: Should two lines for the same SKU be treated as one request for the total? (Yes.)
Should the error still name the SKU that ran short? (Yes, the message is shown to support staff.)
Can I change the function’s shape? (Keep the signature; callers depend on it.)
orient: Read the README rules: “an order is all or nothing” is the promise that broke.
Ran the suite first: everything passed, so the bug lives in a case the tests do not cover.
Searched for “OutOfStock” to see who raises it: Stock.remove and fulfil. fulfil is the entry point for orders.
trace: Hypothesis: the check runs per line, not per SKU. The first loop compares 2 with 3 twice and passes both times.
The second loop removes 2 mugs, then Stock.remove raises on the next line, after the first removal has happened.
Confirmed with a print of stock.quantity("mug") inside the except branch: 1, not 3.
wrapUp: Cause: the up-front check looked at each line alone, so repeated SKUs could pass the check together and fail halfway through removal.
Fix: total the lines per SKU first, check the totals, then remove. Two small loops, same signature and error message.
Trade-off: a dict per order is extra memory, which is negligible at order sizes.
With more time: give Stock a reserve/commit API so the all-or-nothing rule lives in one place.
Noticed but not changed: fulfil does not reject zero or negative quantities itself; it relies on Stock.remove.

tasks.title: Low-stock report
brief: The buyers want a reorder list. Add Stock.low(threshold), returning (sku, quantity) pairs for every SKU at or below the threshold.
Lowest quantity first, ties broken by SKU name. SKUs that have sold out (quantity 0) must still appear. A negative threshold is a mistake and should raise ValueError.
done: Stock.low(threshold) returns sorted (sku, quantity) pairs, threshold inclusive.
Sold-out SKUs are included; an empty stockroom gives an empty list.
A negative threshold raises ValueError, matching how add and remove validate input.

questions: Is the threshold inclusive? (Yes: “at or below”.)
Pairs or just SKUs? (Pairs, so the buyer sees how low.)
Should SKUs never added at all appear? (No, only SKUs the stockroom knows about.)
orient: Stock is one small class; skus() is the closest existing pattern (it sorts its output).
Checked how errors are signalled: add and remove raise ValueError for bad input, so low should too.
Ran the suite for a baseline: all green.
walkthrough.failingTest:
def test_low_lists_lowest_first():
    stock = Stock()
    stock.add("mug", 5)
    stock.add("bowl", 1)
    stock.add("cup", 2)
    assert stock.low(2) == [("bowl", 1), ("cup", 2)]  # AttributeError before the change
trace: Data lives in self._levels, a dict of SKU to level. Removing to zero keeps the key, so sold-out SKUs are still there to report.
Sorting by (quantity, sku) gives lowest first with a stable, readable tie-break.
wrapUp: Added Stock.low with input validation that mirrors add and remove, plus a visible test.
Checked by hand: threshold 0 lists only sold-out SKUs, a big threshold lists everything, an empty stockroom gives [].
With more time: let the buyer set a per-SKU reorder point instead of one threshold.
Noticed but not changed: skus() and low() both sort; if the stockroom grew large, a sorted structure would help.
